newsitem.title: USA: Phillips nears deal on Texas refinery upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Phillips nears deal on Texas refinery upgrade.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co is nearing a deal with state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA on a joint venture to upgrade the U.S. major's Sweeney, Texas refinery, Phillips Chairman Wayne Allen said on Thursday.
The deal, valued at $400 million to $500 million, would include the addition of a coker at the 185,000 barrel per day refinery to process a heavy Venezuelan crude slate, Allen said.

"It's (a) four or five hundred million dollars, highly financed joint venture," Allen said of the deal. "It's attractive, though, because it gives us some capability to run the heavier crudes and optimize our crude slate."
Phillips in January confirmed talks with the Corpoven unit of PDVSA to upgrade the Sweeney refinery, including the addition of a coker unit, and Allen would only say that a deal is expected "soon"..

The upgrade is part of the Bartlesville, Okla.-based company's push to boost refining margins and position its refining operations for an ongoing consolidation in the domestic downstream business, he said.

"We don't plan to exit the business, so we approach it like we are going to keep it forever. Obviously, if there was a business opportunity where we could spread our overheads over a larger volume base, we would do it," he said.
"That's really what these alliances and mergers are all about," he said.

For its part, PDVSA is seeking to add up to 800,000 barrels per day (bpd) of U.S. refining capacity to its existing 1 million bpd capacity, which would make the Venezuelan company the largest U.S. refiner.

A power outage at the Sweeney petrochemical complex trimmed refining and chemical earnings by $21 million in the second quarter, offsetting what would have been a "blowout quarter" for Phillips refining, marketing and transportation segment, Allen said.

Phillips posted $307 million, or $1.17 a share net income in the second quarter, up from $221 million or $0.84 a share in the same period last year. Total revenues fell to $3.8 billion from $4 billion in the same period last year.
